message.content:
Based on my search, here is the information about the maximum unemployment benefits in Massachusetts:

## Maximum Weekly Benefit Amount

As of **October 2025**, the maximum weekly unemployment benefit in Massachusetts is **$1,105 per week** for new claims. This increased from $1,051 at the start of October 2025.

## Additional Dependent Allowance

Massachusetts also offers a dependent allowance of **up to $25 per week for each dependent child**, with a maximum of **$150 extra per week** for dependents. This means the absolute maximum with dependents could reach approximately **$1,105 per week** (the base maximum already appears to account for some dependent allowances in certain sources, though the exact structure varies by source).

## Maximum Duration

Massachusetts offers **up to 30 weeks** of regular unemployment benefits when the unemployment rate in any Massachusetts metropolitan area exceeds 5.1%. Under normal conditions, the duration is **26 weeks**. This makes Massachusetts one of the most generous states in terms of benefit duration.

## Why Massachusetts is Highest

Massachusetts has the highest (or among the highest) maximum weekly unemployment benefits in the nation because:
- State law requires the maximum weekly benefit to be revised annually based on the state's average weekly wage
- The average weekly wage in Massachusetts increased from $1,829.13 to $1,922.48 during the 12-month period ending in March 2025

## Important Notes

- Benefits are calculated as approximately **50% of your average weekly wage** during your base period, subject to the maximum cap
- You must have earned at least $6,000 during your base period to qualify
- The first week of unemployment is typically a waiting week and is not paid
- Benefits are taxable for both federal and Massachusetts state income tax purposes
